The COMETBOARDS optimization tool is written in FORTRAN 77 and is available on Cray, Convex, Iris, and Sun computing platforms.
The cascade optimization strategy in COMETBOARDS involves using multiple optimizers in sequence, with the solution from one optimizer perturbed and used as the starting point for the next optimizer.

For the subsonic aircraft optimization, the final optimum design had a takeoff weight of 199,275.6 lb and had four active constraints: takeoff field length, excess fuel, maximum pressure ratio, and maximum turbine inlet temperature.

The wave-rotor-topped turbofan engine optimization problem was formulated as a sequence of 47 optimization subproblems, one for each mission point defined by Mach number, altitude, and power setting combination.
The active design variables for the wave-rotor engine were the rotor's rotational speed and the heat added, while the key constraints included compressor speed limits and surge margins.

Compared to using NEPP alone, the combined COMETBOARDS-NEPP tool produced higher thrust values across the 47 mission points for the wave-rotor engine, with maximum increases around mission points 12, 26, and 32.

The cascade optimization strategy in COMETBOARDS was able to converge to the same global optimum solution for both the subsonic aircraft and wave-rotor engine problems, even when starting from different initial design points.
COMETBOARDS has a modular organization that allows for the soft-coupling and integration of various analysis tools like FLOPS, NEPP, and RPK_NASTRAN.
Some of the unique features of COMETBOARDS that aided in the optimization of aircraft and engines include the cascade strategy, variable and constraint formulations, and a global scaling strategy.

The combined COMETBOARDS-FLOPS-NEPP design tool eliminates the need for manual intervention in the design of aircraft and air-breathing propulsion engines, making the design process easier and more automated.
